profile.reading:
Csquare IAD2-B sits at 22860 International Drive, Sterling, Virginia 20166, part of Csquare's IAD2 campus in Loudoun County, described by Csquare's own materials as "two additional pods" connected by dark fiber to the nearby IAD1 campus; this building is one of those two pods, per OSM address tagging cross-referenced against Csquare's own IAD spec sheet. Csquare's SEC Form S-1 property table, however, lists only one IAD2 asset, "IAD2_A," treating the whole leased-and-owned IAD2 campus as a single reportable property rather than separately disclosing an "IAD2-B" line item, so this building's individual leasing percentage and square footage are not independently broken out in Csquare's SEC filing the way IAD2-A's are; its existence and address are nonetheless confirmed by Csquare's own spec-sheet documentation and this record's own OSM sourcing. Csquare (formerly branded Centersquare, launched April 2024 by Brookfield Infrastructure to combine Cyxtera and Evoque, AT&T's divested data center business) went public via IPO on NASDAQ in July 2026 at $21.00 per share. Csquare's public spec sheet gives a campus-wide total of 48,169 square feet raised floor, 35.8 megawatts of utility power, 8.5 megawatts of UPS capacity, and 20 megawatts of generator capacity across the IAD2 campus, with SOC 1/2 Type II, PCI-DSS, NIST 800-53 PE High, and ISO 27001 certifications. Csquare does not name a power utility or year-opened date.

Csquare's Sterling, Virginia IAD2 campus sits within Loudoun County's Data Center Alley, the largest concentration of data center capacity in the world. Csquare's SEC S-1 discloses 389 megawatts of total sellable power capacity across its full 64-facility, 21-market portfolio as of March 31, 2026. The dark-fiber link Csquare describes between IAD2 and the nearby IAD1 campus allows customers at either site to interconnect directly without routing traffic through a third-party carrier hotel, a common colocation-industry practice for operators with multiple nearby buildings in the same metro.

sources.title: Csquare, Inc. Form S-1 Registration Statement (IAD2 reported as single asset "IAD2_A")

reading.body:
IAD2-B is one of two pods on Csquare's 48,169-square-foot IAD2 campus in Sterling, Virginia, connected by dark fiber to the nearby IAD1 campus. The campus publishes 35.8 megawatts of utility power, 8.5 megawatts of UPS capacity, and 20 megawatts of generator capacity across both pods. At 40 kilowatts per rack, a common AI training density, 35.8 megawatts of IT load is roughly 900 racks, though the campus's individual pod breakdown and actual IT allocation are not published separately.

The facility holds SOC 1/2 Type II, PCI-DSS, NIST 800-53 PE High, and ISO 27001 certifications, qualifying it for regulated workloads and security-sensitive tenancy. Csquare does not publish which tenants occupy this campus, the year it opened, or the serving utility.

IAD2-B sits in Loudoun County's Data Center Alley, the largest data center concentration in the world. Virginia has 326 mapped data center facilities, 23 with published capacity figures totaling 1,375 megawatts, and the IAD2 campus ranks 24th in the state by published megawatts. Csquare's full portfolio spans 389 megawatts across 64 facilities in 21 markets as of March 2026, making this campus part of a geographically diversified operator.
